The discussion says the patient started statin therapy in her early thirties, shortly after an acute MI and four coronary stents, whereas the case description starts rosuvastatin after a first endocrinology examination for elevated lipids two years before pregnancy (age 38 at the 10-week visit) and describes angiography and stenting in the same year. The age mismatch is arithmetic only and the case text does not literally order statin start against the MI or stents, so it is an ambiguity, not a source conflict.
The abstract states the cardiomyopathy and angina pectoris diagnoses; the case text mentions anginal pains and coronary narrowing but not ischemic cardiomyopathy.
Blood pressure, edema and proteinuria are described as "thoroughly monitored and in order"; recorded as normal evaluations without asserting that edema or proteinuria were absent.

Ultrasound stigmata of SGA were reported within normal limits during pregnancy while the newborn is described as considered small for gestational age; the two statements refer to different time points and are both kept.
Obesity is named as a possible confounding factor with BMI 27.2 kg/m^(2); the statement is hedged.
